title: “CALL DOWN FIRE?”
paragraphs: “CALL DOWN FIRE?”
That’s what they asked.

Not enemies of God.
Not pagan warlords.
Just… a village that said no to Jesus.
So two men stepped forward.

James the Apostle
John the Apostle

Brothers.
Disciples.
Future pillars of the Church.
But in that moment?
Thunder.
In Gospel of Luke 9, they looked at Jesus Christ and asked:
“Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven and destroy them?”
Let that sink in.

They weren’t joking.
They meant Elijah-level judgment.

🔥 One prayer.
🔥 One blast of heaven.
🔥 One village… gone.

That’s what religious zeal can become
when mercy hasn’t finished its work.
And here’s the shock.
Jesus didn’t applaud them.
He rebuked them.
Not the village.
The disciples.
Because the spirit of the Kingdom is not vengeance—it’s redemption.
Those men wanted fire from heaven.
But Jesus came to bring grace from heaven.
And here’s the twist that wrecks me every time.

The same John who once wanted to burn a village…
later wrote the words:
“God is love.” (1 John 4:8)
Think about that.
Thunder became tenderness.
Judgment turned into mercy.
Why?
Because when you walk long enough with Jesus, He burns something else instead.
Not cities.

Pride.
Anger.
Self-righteous fire.
He replaces it with a different flame.
The fire of the Holy Spirit.
Listen carefully, friend.
Some of us still pray like the Sons of Thunder.

“Lord, judge them.”
“Lord, expose them.”
“Lord, destroy them.”
But Jesus whispers:
“I came to save them.”

That includes the people who rejected you.
Mocked you.
Closed the door on you.
And maybe… it includes you too.
Because the Gospel is this:

The fire of God that should have fallen on us
fell instead on Christ at the cross.
That’s why mercy is still flowing today.

So if you feel like thunder—
anger boiling, judgment rising—
Bring it to Jesus.
Let Him turn your fire into light.
Because Jesus still rewrites everything.
Someone out there thinks God only has fire left for them.
But the cross says otherwise.
